newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-SERIE A RACE MAY BE DECIDED IN BIG MAY 18 CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SERIE A RACE MAY BE DECIDED IN BIG MAY 18 CLASH.

text.p: The race for the Italian championship could be decided when leaders Juventus and second-placed Parma clash on May 18 after Juve slipped up at the weekend and allowed their chief rival to peg them back.
On Sunday, Parma closed the gap at the top of Serie A to four points with five games still to play when they won 2-1 away to Atalanta. Juventus were held to a 0-0 home draw by Sampdoria.
Prior to meeting Juventus in Turin in two weeks time, Parma have home games against Vicenza and AC Milan while Juventus are away to Verona and at home to Piacenza.
If both sides pick up good results in those games, then the title race would still be up for grabs when the two meet at the Stadio Delle Alpi.
For their final two games of the season, Juventus visit Atalanta and host Lazio while Parma are at home to Bologna and away to Verona.
Despite that 2-1 win on Sunday, Parma coach Carlo Ancelotti believes his side should concentrate on ensuring second place and a consequent Champions League qualification.
"The last time we set our sights on Juventus, we got burned up (in a 2-0 home defeat by Udinese)... For now, let's concentrate on extending our lead over Inter," he said.
Parma are four points clear of third placed Inter Milan, their only realistic rival for second place.
Ancelotti's opposite number, Juventus coach Marcello Lippi, remained philosophic about the title contest following the draw with Sampdoria.
"We always knew that Parma might do this (close the gap) and we never said that it would be easy for us to win the championship," he said.
